DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri).

Based on your age, the 3-week history of occipital and retro-orbital headaches, and the progression of vision loss described as blurriness and peripheral field cuts, combined with the likely findings of bilateral papilledema on the fundoscopy, this clinical picture is classic for IIH. This condition typically affects women of childbearing age or older women, often associated with obesity, though it can occur without other systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss. Have you experienced any pulsatile tinnitus (a rhythmic whooshing sound in your ears) recently?
